correctness.rationale: For the unsigned incidence M, simplicity and characteristic two give B=MᵀM, and T=MMᵀ is the sum of I+R_a over the generators. These commuting summands square to zero, so T²=0 and B³=0. The group algebra is the truncated square-zero coordinate algebra: T multiplies by t with linear part indexed by c=⊕S. If c≠0, complete t to independent degree-one coordinates. The induced endomorphism is well-defined because augmentation elements square to zero; invertibility on degree one implies generation on the associated graded and hence invertibility of the filtered map. Multiplication by the first coordinate has rank v/2 and equal kernel and image. Connectedness gives H=im M the zero-sum hyperplane (path column sums generate all e_u+e_v) and ker Mᵀ the all-one line in H, so rank B=v−2. For an independent check of the key compression, take a binary linear functional f on vertices with f(c)=1. Then Tf=1 and f∈H since it has 2^(r−1) ones, even for r≥2. Symmetry implies ker T⊂H, so dim T(H)=v/2−1, and Tf=1 gives a further one-dimensional loss under Mᵀ. Thus rank B²=v/2−2. The ranks force (a_3,a_2,a_1)=(v/2−2,2,(s−3)v/2+2), including v=4 where s=2. Kernel-size differences give extinction populations (with exactly one state at time zero). U=I+B has U²=I+B² and U⁴=I, and its fixed subspaces at 1 and 2 give the primitive periods and orbit counts; q is any finite characteristic-two field size. In the excluded K_{4,4} boundary, the rook adjacency squares to zero by J_4²=0.
